safety_verdicts.content: Patient has tingling and numbness in the shoulder.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies tingling/numbness also felt on the shoulder; generated mentions shoulder pain but does not clearly document shoulder tingling/numbness.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting shoulder tingling/numbness can reduce accurate neurologic localization (e.g., radicular vs plexus vs central process) and may slightly weaken the documentation of symptom extent/progression. However, other key neuro symptoms (hand numbness/weakness and transient visual loss) are still captured, so immediate safety impact is limited.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states the patient reports headaches; generated only includes headache as a safety-net trigger, not as a reported symptom.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document headaches can miss an important red-flag accompanying focal neurologic symptoms and transient visual loss, potentially affecting triage/urgency and differential diagnosis (e.g., migraine vs vascular/ICP-related causes). Even though headache is mentioned as a return precaution, not recording it as a present symptom could lead to underestimation of risk in downstream care.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states patient denies neck pain; generated ROS does not address neck pain.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting denial of neck pain mainly reduces completeness of the ROS and may slightly affect consideration of cervical radiculopathy, but it is unlikely to change immediate management given the broader neurologic concern. This is primarily documentation quality loss without clear direct harm.
